citeinfo.title: SPARROW model inputs and simulated streamflow, nutrient and suspended-sediment loads in streams of the Southeastern United States, 2012 Base Year
Spatially Referenced Models of Streamflow and Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Suspended-Sediment Loads in Streams of the Southeastern United States
citeinfo.geoform: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2019-5135

descript.abstract: The U.S. Geological Survey's (USGS) SPAtially Referenced Regression On Watershed attributes (SPARROW) model was used to aid in the interpretation of monitoring data and simulate streamflow and water-quality conditions in streams across the Southeast Region of the United States. SPARROW is a hybrid empirical/process-based mass balance model that can be used to estimate the major sources and environmental factors that affect the long-term supply, transport, and fate of contaminants in streams. The spatially explicit model structure is defined by a river reach network coupled with contributing catchments. The model is calibrated by statistically relating watershed sources and transport-related properties to monitoring-based water-quality load estimates. This USGS data release includes input and output files associated with 2012 SPARROW simulations of streamflow, total nitrogen, total phosphorus and suspended-sediment load in streams of the Southeast region. Model construction, calibration and results are described in Hoos and Roland (2019, https://doi.org/10.3133/sir20195135).
descript.purpose: This USGS data release contains all of the input and output files needed to reproduce the model results described in Hoos and Roland (2019). Model input and output text files provided here can be linked (via the comid attribute) to the shapefiles that are also provided for displaying data as maps.

citeinfo.title: Database of modified routing for NHDPlus version 2.1 flowlines: ENHDPlusV2_us

srcinfo.srccontr: The database (ENHDPlusV2_us) contains a topologically reconditioned (enhanced) version of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) and the USGS NHDPlus Version 2.1 (NHDPlusV2) flowline network. This enhanced version of the drainage network has improved accuracy in networking capabilities used to identify the incremental watershed for each reach (the area that drains directly to a reach without passing through another reach). The ENHDPlusV2_us database also includes attributes for surface-water features, such as streams (identified as perennial or intermittent), lakes, ponds, and artificial reservoirs and attributes to define instream/reservoir decay (delivery fraction).

enttyp.enttypd: This is the SPARROW model input data file also referred to as the sparrow_data1 file. This data file contains one record for each stream segment in the Southeast 2012 SPARROW modeled river basins. Input attributes include: network, source, land-to-water delivery, instream and in-reservoir decay characteristics of the stream segment and its associated incremental watershed. Also included are attributes representing monitored streamflow and nutrient and suspended-sediment load, which are used as model calibration targets.
